specification.problem: Discrete-time coined quantum walk on a 4-site open chain with i.i.d. dynamic edge percolation. Each step applies U_omega = S_omega (I x C) for a random edge configuration omega in {0,1}^3. The averaged dynamics is the random unitary channel Phi, and the long-time limit of Phi^n is the projection onto its peripheral eigenspace. Predict the asymptotic state and position distribution, then compare with a finite-n circuit simulation.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: 4 positions (2 qubits), 1 coin qubit, 3 edge ancillas, 6 qubits total, Hadamard coin, localized initial walker, edge-open probability p. Covers (a) exact classical construction of U_omega and the superoperator with peripheral spectrum, and (b) a circuit simulation of n steps with fresh ancillas per step, reading the position distribution. Outside scope: the paper's general finite-graph theory, the detailed 1D chain classification, the numerical example in the paper, and the 2D lattice Grover-coin results. These cannot be reconstructed from the abstract.

equations.label: Random unitary channel
equations.description: The one-step map averaged over independent edge configurations.
equations.abstract_quote: applying the asymptotic methods concerning random unitary maps
equations.justification: The abstract says the long-time limit is treated with random unitary map methods. The explicit i.i.d. form is a modelling assumption taken from the sketch.
assumptions: Edges are independent with equal p

equations.label: Coined step with reflection
equations.latex: S_\omega|x,c\rangle=\begin{cases}|x+s_c,c\rangle & \text{edge } e(x,c)\text{ open}\\ |x,1-c\rangle & \text{closed or boundary}\end{cases},\quad s_0=+1,\ s_1=-1,\ U_\omega=S_\omega(I\otimes C)
equations.description: The edge e(x,c) is the one between x and x+s_c. The shift moves the walker if the edge is open and reflects with a coin flip if it is closed. Boundary sites behave as closed edges, so the shift is a permutation and hence unitary.
equations.justification: This is the proposed concrete implementation of reflecting dynamic percolation on the chain. The abstract does not specify it.
assumptions: Boundary acts as a closed edge

equations.label: Ancilla preparation
equations.description: Each edge ancilla is prepared so that measuring it gives open with probability p. Fresh ancillas are used each step.
assumptions: Fresh ancilla per step, or ancillas reset to |0>

equations.label: Peripheral eigen-condition and limit
equations.latex: \Phi(X)=\lambda X,\ |\lambda|=1\iff U_\omega XU_\omega^\dagger=\lambda X\ \forall\omega;\quad \Phi^n\to P_{\rm per}\ (n\to\infty)
equations.description: For a random unitary channel on a finite-dimensional space, the peripheral eigenvectors are the common eigen-operators of all U_omega. The limit of Phi^n is the projection onto this peripheral space.
equations.abstract_quote: applying the asymptotic methods concerning random unitary maps
equations.justification: This is the standard result for random unitary channels. The abstract only names the method, so the specific statement comes from background knowledge.

equations.label: Position readout
equations.description: The position distribution after n steps equals the position-qubit measurement distribution in the circuit with ancillas traced out or refreshed each step. The comparison target is P_infty(x)=sum_c <x,c|P_per(rho_0)|x,c>. It is expected to be uniform (1/4) if the only peripheral element is the identity, which is a conjecture for the generic case.
equations.justification: The readout follows from the sketch. Uniformity should be checked numerically and not assumed.

registers.name: edge
registers.role: edge-open ancillas, one per edge, refreshed each step

specification.initial_state: |x_0=0>|c_0=0> on pos and coin, with all edge ancillas in |0>

steps.description: Classically build the eight U_omega as 8x8 matrices, form the superoperator sum_omega p(omega) U_omega conj(U_omega), and find its eigenvalues of modulus 1 and their eigenvectors.

Per circuit step: apply Ry(theta) to each edge ancilla and the Hadamard on the coin. Then apply the shift controlled on the coin and the edge ancilla, using multi-controlled increment/decrement, with X on the coin for the reflection branch.

Discard the ancillas, either with new ancillas per step (which needs more than 6 qubits) or by resetting them. Repeat for n steps and take the position distribution. Compare it with the classical Phi^n evolution and with P_infty.

specification.measurement: Measure only the 2 position qubits after n steps. Under the little-endian convention, bits[::-1][i] is position bit i. The ancillas are reset or averaged out.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute the peripheral spectrum and fixed points of the 64x64 superoperator. Compute P_infty and compare it with the empirical P_n(x) as n grows.
assumptions: Chosen instance: 4-site open chain, Hadamard coin, independent edges with equal p (e.g. p=0.5), localized initial state
The long-time limit is approximated by finite n
Reusing the 3 ancillas by reset gives 6 qubits; fresh ancillas per step exceed the cap, so use mid-circuit reset or classical averaging over omega
